newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-BRILLIANT PRICE LEAVES FIELD IN HIS WAKE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BRILLIANT PRICE LEAVES FIELD IN HIS WAKE.

text.p: Former world number one Nick Price fired a second successive 66 on Saturday to take a five-shot lead into the final round of the Dimension Data Pro-Am.
Price finished the third round on 199, 17 under par, to lead from Irishman Padraig Harrington who birdied the last hole to complete a 68 for a total of 204.
One shot further back were South Africa's David Frost and Denmark's Thomas Bjorn who both carded disappointing 71's after beginning the round just one shot behind Price.
Price was one of a group of 80 players who had to complete his second round early in the morning after lightning halted play on Friday.

The 40-year-old Zimbabwean was six under par with nine holes left to play and covered the back nine at the Gary Player Country Club in 31 strokes, five under par, taking him to 11 under for the tournament.

In the afternoon he continued his brilliant form with birdies on the first two holes to put daylight between himself and the rest of the field. He went out in 32, meaning that at that stage he had covered the 18 holes in 63 during the day.
Price had two more birdies at 10 and 11 to go to 17 under and then played par golf on the way home.

Harrington was out in 33, but could not find any more inspiration on the back nine until a birdie at the last. But his efforts have put him into real contention for a Ryder Cup spot at the end of the year.

After splitting the first two rounds between Country Club and Lost City, the final two rounds are being played at the former, the home of the Million Dollar Challenge which Price won with a record 24 under par in 1993.
One man who experienced the highs and lows of the game in one round was veteran American Bruce Vaughan. Starting at the 10th, Vaughan birdied six holes in a row and covered the stretch in 29 shots.

He made his his eighth birdie on the first, his 10th, but then fell to earth with a crash. He made bogey six at the par five second, bogey four at the short seventh and a disastrous triple bogey seven at the next. He came home in 40 for an 18 hole score of 69.
